claims.text: Random atomic distributions in HfNbTaTiZr cause severe lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr produces wavy <111>{110} edge-dislocation cores.
Wavy edge-dislocation cores reduce edge-dislocation mobility.
Reduced edge-dislocation mobility gives HfNbTaTiZr a more stable elevated-temperature elastic response than conventional alloys.
Reduced edge-dislocation mobility alters the elevated-temperature thermal expansion of HfNbTaTiZr.
Controlled arc melting and subsequent heat treatment produce a homogenized, single-phase BCC HfNbTaTiZr initial state.
The proposed measurements are performed at room temperature, 500°C, 700°C, and 900°C.
A strain rate of approximately 1 × 10^-4 s^-1 matches that used in the cited elevated-temperature refractory-HEA study.
Heterogeneous atomic radii, especially the inclusion of Hf, produce compositional fluctuations and severe lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortions displace edge-dislocation cores from their neutral planes.
Displaced edge-dislocation cores move more slowly and thereby limit normal high-temperature softening.
The proposed core modification determines the temperature evolution of elastic anisotropy and thermal expansion.
Relative to a less-distorted conventional refractory-alloy baseline, HfNbTaTiZr will show a more gradual decrease in yield strength with temperature.
The Zener anisotropy ratio of HfNbTaTiZr will change from approximately 1.2 at room temperature to approximately 1.6 at 900°C.
HfNbTaTiZr will exhibit anomalous thermal expansion attributable to constrained dislocation mobility.
The comparator consists of BCC refractory HEAs or BCC alloys with similar processing but less lattice distortion.
The hypothesis is expected to apply from ambient temperature through 900°C at strain rates near 1 × 10^-4 s^-1.
Substantially different temperatures or strain rates may produce behavior outside the hypothesis.
The hypothesis predicts dominance of <111>{110} edge dislocations rather than screw dislocations.
A lack of significant differences from the conventional-alloy baseline, or observed screw-dislocation dominance, is designated as falsifying the hypothesis.
